classification.difficultyReason: Identify the complete diagonal to establish the common sum, then select rows, columns or diagonals with one unknown and subtract their known entries in a workable order.

content.prompt: Complete the following magic squares, in which each row, column and diagonal must add up to the same sum.

inlines.text: The complete diagonal gives the common sum:
Use the other diagonal, then the rows and columns:
Every row, column and diagonal sums to

answer.worked:
The complete diagonal gives the common sum:
$$\begin{align*}S&=2\frac45+2\frac{7}{10}+2\frac35\\&=\frac{28}{10}+\frac{27}{10}+\frac{26}{10}\\&=8\frac{1}{10}.\end{align*}$$
Use the other diagonal, then the rows and columns:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bottom right}&=\frac{81}{10}-3-\frac{27}{10}=2\frac25\\\text{Top middle}&=\frac{81}{10}-3-\frac{14}{5}=2\frac{3}{10}\\\text{Middle left}&=\frac{81}{10}-3-\frac{13}{5}=2\frac12\\\text{Middle right}&=\frac{81}{10}-\frac{14}{5}-\frac{12}{5}=2\frac{9}{10}\\\text{Bottom middle}&=\frac{81}{10}-\frac{13}{5}-\frac{12}{5}=3\frac{1}{10}.\end{align*}$$
Every row, column and diagonal sums to $8\frac{1}{10}$.
